A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable presentations of the same GAPrompt study, including Appendices A–C. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original point-cloud classification experiments and ablations, supplemented by sensitivity analyses and feature visualizations in Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains the original GAPrompt classification results, ablations and appendix analyses. These remain original empirical results despite being unchanged from v1.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Appendix B retain the same Point Prompt, Point Shift Prompter, Prompt Propagation, adapter enhancement and downstream prediction procedures.

E1.justification: Both evaluate point-cloud classification on ModelNet40 and the OBJ_BG, OBJ_ONLY and PB_T50_RS variants of ScanObjectNN. No datasets, tasks or distinct test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figure 9 retain the same comparators, including IDPT, DAPT, Point-PEFT and the NLP/2D PEFT methods. The corrected IDPT citation and added background references do not change the evaluated comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same backbones, metrics and settings, including 2048 ScanObjectNN input points, 1024 ModelNet40 points, evaluation without voting and the training configurations in Table 5.

E4.justification: Tables 3–4, Figures 4–10 and Appendix C retain the same component, propagation, prompt initialization/count, enhancement-factor and head-input ablations, alongside attention, shifted-cloud and t-SNE analyses.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates without repeated-run counts, specified seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, GAPrompt remains at 90.67% on PB_T50_RS with Point-FEMAE and 96.2% on ModelNet40 with PointGPT-L in Table 1.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(23) are unchanged, including the attention decomposition in Section 3.4 and distance-weighted feature interpolation in Appendix B.2. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same three-component contribution and claims of superior PEFT performance, competitive full-fine-tuning accuracy and substantially fewer trainable parameters.

C2.justification: The explanations involving geometric awareness, prompt-injection randomness, shifted-point compactness and complementary shape features remain unchanged. The main text and Appendix C introduce no new limitations or applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B retain the same hyperparameters and implementation details, including the single RTX 4090 and PyTorch 1.13.1 disclosure. The code-availability statement and repository link also remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds InsVP (Liu et al., 2024) and CAPrompt (Li and Zhou, 2025). It replaces the unrelated face-super-resolution IDPT reference by Shi et al. (2022) with the point-cloud prompting work by Zha et al. (2023). The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Acknowledgments now precede the Impact Statement, and the proceedings label changes from the 41st to the 42nd conference. The scientific narrative and appendix organization otherwise remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: The bibliography reflows across pages 9–10, and the acknowledgments and impact-statement blocks exchange positions. All ten figures and five tables retain their content, captions, structure and placement.

improvement.justification: V3 corrects the mismatched IDPT attribution in the introduction and Section 2.2, replacing a face-super-resolution reference with the relevant point-cloud prompting paper. This improves scholarly accuracy, while two added prompting references modestly broaden context. The method, empirical evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
